mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as it reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, with no regime dependency.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 300) triggers expectations of aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 300 (p-value > 0.05 for negative return probability).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signal weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS does not produce negative returns in > 60% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate).

mechanism_narrative: In a low unemployment regime (UNRATE < 3.5%), a decline in unemployment signals economic overheating and aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not negative in > 60% of instances when UNRATE < 3.5% and declining (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate).

mechanism_narrative: Higher industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust economic activity, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO is above 100 (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate (year-over-year) below 1.0% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when GDPC1 growth < 1.0% (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate).

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), a rise in the federal funds rate signals continued aggressive policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not negative in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and rising (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in non-farm payrolls below 50,000 (PAYEMS growth < 50) signals a softening labor market, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS growth < 50 (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate).
